bullets.title: NVDA: Morgan Stanley raises PT to $288 on neocloud revenue-sharing model; UBS expects $3-4B FQ2 beat
bullets.body: MS sees NVDA's neocloud GPU-hour backstop strategy generating $10s of billions in ~100% gross-margin recurring revenue, with 5 GW deployment implying ~$37bn incremental revenue and 7-10% FY29 EPS upside; PT $288 (28% upside, 22x CY27E). UBS separately expects NVDA to beat FQ2 by $3-4B (~$94-95B actual), guides FQ3 to $107-108B, raises CY27 GPU units to 10.8MM and EPS path to $15+ CY27/$20 CY28; maintains Buy at $280 PT. NVDA also announced $500B AI financing platform with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, KKR; Feynman (H2 2028) moving to TSMC A16 process with CPO.

bullets.title: SNDK: Bull case builds post-Investor Day; JPM upgrades to OW, Citi Buy ($2,100 PT), Mizuho $1,900
bullets.body: SNDK guided FY28-30 to mid-to-high teens revenue growth, ~80% GM / ~75% OM / ~50% FCF margins with 100% excess FCF return; 8 customers signed NBMs covering ~66% of bits by FY27 with 4-year visibility. Flash market projected at $300B in 2026 and $500B in 2027. JPMorgan resumed OW at $2,250; GS raised PT to $2,200; Citi reiterates Buy at $2,100; Mizuho raises to $1,900 on HBF upside. Stock +7% premarket.

bullets.title: MU: New Street Research upgrades to Buy with $1,250 PT (32% upside) on memory cycle
bullets.body: Pierre Ferragu at New Street initiated a Buy on MU with a $1,250 price target implying 32% upside from ~$950. MU was also +3.1% premarket alongside broader memory strength from SNDK Investor Day and AI DRAM demand narrative. FactSet consensus PT is $1,549 with a wide $361-$2,200 range.

bullets.title: RDDT: S&P 500 inclusion (Aug 18) drives +10-11% premarket surge; index buy demand ~12.8M shares
bullets.body: Reddit will replace AvalonBay (AVB) in the S&P 500 effective before market open August 18. JPM estimates net indexer demand of 12.8M shares representing ~211% of average daily volume. RDDT becomes only the second pure-play social media name in the index. Average users dipped 2% in July vs June but improved through month-end per Piper.

bullets.title: FOXA: Dual upgrade to OW at JPMorgan ($82 PT) and Wells Fargo ($80 PT) on ROKU deal + strong Tubi
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgraded FOXA from Neutral to Overweight with PT raised to $82 (25% upside) on strong beat-and-raise earnings plus ROKU acquisition rationale; Tubi revenue +35% YoY in F4Q, ROKU platform revenue +25% YoY vs 20% guidance. $400M cost synergy target seen as reasonable at 2% of pro-forma revenue. Wells Fargo upgraded simultaneously to OW at $80. FOXA +2.2-2.7% premarket.

bullets.title: ROKU: Downgraded to EW at Wells Fargo; PT cut to $165 as part of FOXA-ROKU deal announcement
bullets.body: Wells Fargo downgraded ROKU to equal weight from overweight and cut PT to $165 from $167, citing the pending Fox acquisition. The 34% premium to ROKU's unaffected price was deemed a reasonable control premium. ROKU advertising gross margin at 62% with ~82% incremental margins cited as attractive for FOXA.

bullets.title: CSCO: HSBC downgrades to hold, cuts PT to $120 from $137 (6% upside); stock post-earnings disappointment
bullets.body: HSBC cut CSCO to Hold from Buy, trimming PT to $120 from $137, implying only 6% upside from ~$113. This comes after Cisco reportedly disappointed on AI data-center sales projections. FactSet consensus PT is $138.71.

bullets.title: NVDA Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics now in full production; supply chain: TSM (SiPh), LITE (lasers), COHR (optical), GLW, FN
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm NVIDIA's Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics scale-out networking infrastructure has entered full production. TSM handles silicon photonics fab via COUPE process; LITE supplies ELS/high-power lasers and optical alignment & test; COHR provides ELS and optical components; GLW supplies fiber/connectors; FN handles switch CPO assembly & test. Read-through is incrementally positive for LITE, COHR, GLW, FN as supply chain beneficiaries.

bullets.title: LITE/COHR: Q4 FY26 earnings strongly positive; COHR trades $10B lower on 2x revenue, LITE seen as cycle-defining name
bullets.body: COHR Q4 FY26 revenue reached $2.05B (+34% YoY, +13% QoQ), described as strongly positive. Twitter commentary notes COHR generates 2x LITE revenue but trades at a ~$10B lower valuation due to margin mix differences. JPM hosting analyst callback with Joe Cardoso on both names 8/14 at 10am ET. Citi webcast on US import ban on Chinese optical components also scheduled, identifying COHR, CIEN, ANET as potential winners.

bullets.title: APP: JPM initiates Neutral at $400 PT; Piper cautious on publisher payment pressures; higher cash drag flagged
bullets.body: JPM initiates APP at Neutral (Dec-27 PT $400, 18x 2028E EPS $22.42), projecting 2026 net ad revenue of $8.1B (+48%) and 2027 of $9.9B (+22%). Gaming TAM grew only +2% in 2025; APP holds ~70% of mobile gaming mediation. Piper separately flagged higher publisher payments dragging cash from operations as a downgrade factor. APP maintained at Neutral at both JPM and GS ($400 PT).

bullets.title: SHOP: Piper bullish on 2Q margin structure and HQ move to Nevada positioning for S&P 500 inclusion
bullets.body: Piper flagged SHOP's better 2Q margins driven by lower employee costs (-$5MM YoY) and AI token cost management as structural positives. SHOP's Nevada HQ move positions it well for a future S&P 500 addition. No explicit rating given but characterized as bullish read-through on operational efficiency.

bullets.title: AAPL: Trains China-specific LLM with BABA; opens Houston manufacturing center for Mac mini/AI servers
bullets.body: Reuters reported Apple developed a China-specific LLM in partnership with Alibaba rather than licensing Alibaba's model outright. Separately, Apple opened an Advanced Manufacturing Center in Houston investing hundreds of millions; first AI servers shipped and Mac mini production beginning this year. CMA in UK advancing investigation on Apple's steering conduct requirements and NFC fees. KeyBanc maintains UW at $250; July iPhone +19% YoY but pull-forward risk signals potential 2H weakness.

bullets.title: BABA: Sells Lingxi Interactive Entertainment gaming unit for >$1.5B; earnings call Aug 20
bullets.body: Alibaba is close to selling Lingxi Interactive Entertainment to Trustar Capital for over $1.5B (HK$11.77B), continuing its non-core asset divestiture program. BABA earnings call is scheduled for August 20 at 7:30pm ET. Twitter commentary also highlighted BABA's regulatory compliance as a constructive step.

bullets.title: INTC: Upsizes equity offering to $20B at $95; institutional demand exceeded $100B, CEO invests $12M personally
bullets.body: Intel upsized its equity offering from $15B to $20B at $95/share (~2.6% discount) with institutional demand reportedly exceeding $100B; CEO personally subscribed ~$12M. GF Securities reiterates Buy at $136 PT, viewing the offering as a positive signal on management confidence in the foundry/EMIB strategy. Hedgeye flags INTC returning to bullish trend.

bullets.title: EQIX/DLR: Record bookings on AI inference demand; tower multiples hit 10-year lows; HSBC upgrades DLR
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley highlights EQIX and DLR reporting record bookings and backlogs driven by AI inference demand and supply constraints from NIMBYism and supply chain issues. Data center operators benefiting from pricing power and capacity expansion. Tower multiples have compressed ~10 turns as 10-year yields rose from 1.7% to 4.6%; HSBC upgrades DLR to buy. GEV, VRT named by UBS as Buy-rated industrials for AI infrastructure exposure.

bullets.title: CHTR: Receives final approval to acquire Cox Communications for $21.9B
bullets.body: Charter Communications received the final state regulatory approval needed to acquire Cox Communications for $21.9B, with concessions including low-cost internet requirements. The deal includes one of the largest cable consolidations in years. CHTR +reflected in premarket sentiment around the approval.

bullets.title: W (Wayfair): Bernstein upgrades to outperform, raises PT to $125 from $100 (24% upside)
bullets.body: Bernstein analyst Nikhil Devnani upgraded Wayfair to outperform from market perform, raising the price target to $125 from $100 (24% upside). W was +4% premarket. FactSet average target is $122.54 with a $63-$156 range.

bullets.title: NVDA: Samsung Giheung R&D fab to be repurposed to meet NVDA production demand; Feynman ahead of schedule on TSMC A16
bullets.body: Multiple reports indicate Samsung is converting its Giheung R&D fab to support Nvidia's production capacity needs. Additionally, DigiTimes confirms Nvidia's Feynman next-generation platform is ahead of schedule, targeting TSMC A16 (upgraded 2nm) with co-packaged optics and custom HBM integration for H2 2028 mass production.

bullets.title: MDB: Launches managed MCP server; SaaS sector re-rates +8% WoW on WDAY take-private chatter
bullets.body: MongoDB launched a managed MCP server, a positive for its developer platform positioning. Separately, Silver Lake take-private talks for Workday (WDAY) at ~$55B EV ($230-240/share at ~30% premium) drove a broad SaaS floor-multiple re-rating. Wolfe All-SaaS index multiples up 8.26% WoW; IGV -2.8% YTD vs S&P +14%. Piper notes AI market spending data remains constructive with July ad spend +130bps above estimates.

bullets.title: AMD: Raises $4.75B in largest-ever bond offering; deepens AI inference bet via Taalas deal
bullets.body: AMD completed a $4.75B bond offering, its largest-ever U.S. dollar deal, bringing YTD TMT debt issuance to $331B. AMD also deepened its AI inference strategy through a Taalas acquisition and partnered with Cerebras on AI deployment. HBM and CoWoS supply constraints continue to favor AMD and NVDA as ASICs struggle to secure capacity.
